extracted.intended_audience: students of mathematical logic / computability theory (advanced undergraduate or graduate)
extracted.subtask_description: Definitions, closure properties, examples, and constructions for primitive recursive functions and relations; includes coding of sequences/trees and various recursion schemas used to show many natural functions are primitive recursive.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition 133A: primitive recursion schema
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To define a (k+1)-place function by primitive recursion give the base value at 0 via f and the successor-step via g which may use the immediately preceding value h(...,y). Examples: add and mult are given by this pattern (add fixes one argument and recurses on the other).

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition 133B: composition
rubrics_metrics.description: If f is k-place and g0,...,gk−1 are n-place, define h(x0,...,xn−1) = f(g0(...), ..., gk−1(...)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Composition yields a new n-place function by computing the gi's on the input and feeding results to f. Projection functions allow omission, reordering, or duplication of arguments (e.g., h(x)=add(x,x) via projections).

rubrics_metrics.name: Primitive base functions: zero, succ, projections
rubrics_metrics.description: Include zero(x)=0, succ(x)=x+1, and projection functions P^n_i(x0,...,xn−1)=xi for each n and i<n.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These basic functions form the foundation from which other primitive recursive functions are built by composition and primitive recursion; constants can be built from zero and succ.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition 133C: primitive recursive functions (inductive closure)
rubrics_metrics.description: The set of primitive recursive functions is the smallest set containing zero, succ, and all projection functions and closed under composition and primitive recursion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Equivalently defined by stages S0 (basic functions) and Si+1 (apply one composition or primitive recursion to functions in Si); union of stages yields the full class.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stage construction for primitive recursive functions
rubrics_metrics.description: S0 = {zero, succ, projections}; Si+1 is all functions obtained by applying a single composition or primitive recursion to functions in Si; S = ⋃_{i∈N} Si.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use stage notation to enumerate/organize primitive recursive functions and to prove closure properties inductively.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notation system for constructions (Comp and Rec)
rubrics_metrics.description: Notation Comp_{k,n}[F, G0, ..., G_{k−1}] denotes composition; Rec_k[F,G] (or Rec[F,G]) denotes the function defined by primitive recursion from F and G.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These symbolic notations allow systematic enumeration and coding of primitive recursive functions (used later to assign numeric codes to notations).

rubrics_metrics.name: Primitive recursive functions are computable
rubrics_metrics.description: If f and g in a primitive recursion definition are computable, then the defined function h is computable; composition of computable functions is computable, and basic functions are computable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hence every primitive recursive function is computable; computing h(⃗x,y) proceeds by successively computing h(⃗x,0), h(⃗x,1), ..., h(⃗x,y).

rubrics_metrics.name: Addition is primitive recursive
rubrics_metrics.description: add(x0,0)=x0; add(x0,y+1)=succ(add(x0,y)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Here f(x0)=P^1_0 (the identity) and g(x0,y,z)=succ(z) (defined by composition succ∘P^3_2). This matches the primitive recursion schema.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multiplication is primitive recursive
rubrics_metrics.description: mult(x,0)=0; mult(x,y+1)=add(mult(x,y),x).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Uses add in the recursion step; given add is primitive recursive, mult follows by primitive recursion (proof left as exercise in text).

rubrics_metrics.name: Exponentiation is primitive recursive
rubrics_metrics.description: exp(x,0)=1; exp(x,y+1)=mult(x,exp(x,y)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Officially written with f(x)=1 and g(x,y,z)=mult(x,z) expressed via composition from primitive recursive functions; shows exp(x,y)=x^y is primitive recursive.

rubrics_metrics.name: Predecessor (pred) is primitive recursive
rubrics_metrics.description: pred(0)=0; pred(y+1)=y.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fits awkwardly into schema, so define pred′(x,y) by primitive recursion then compose: pred′(x,0)=0, pred′(x,y+1)=P^3_1(x,y, pred′(x,y)) = y; set pred(y)=pred′(zero(y), P^1_0(y)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Factorial is primitive recursive
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Formally define a two-place helper h(x,0)=1, h(x,y+1)=mult(h(x,y), y+1) and then fac(y)=h(y,y).

rubrics_metrics.name: Truncated subtraction is primitive recursive
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Defines x ˙− y = 0 if x < y, otherwise x − y; uses pred which is primitive recursive, so ˙− is primitive recursive by recursion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distance, max, min are primitive recursive
rubrics_metrics.description: Distance |x−y| = (x ˙− y) + (y ˙− x); max(x,y) = x + (y ˙− x); min similarly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Define by composition from + and truncated subtraction; shows common numeric combinators are primitive recursive.

rubrics_metrics.name: Closure under finite sums and products (Proposition 136H)
rubrics_metrics.description: If f(⃗x,z) is primitive recursive then g(⃗x,y)=Σ_{z=0}^{y} f(⃗x,z) and h(⃗x,y)=Π_{z=0}^{y} f(⃗x,z) are primitive recursive.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Defined by primitive recursion: g(⃗x,0)=f(⃗x,0), g(⃗x,y+1)=g(⃗x,y)+f(⃗x,y+1), and analogously for products.

rubrics_metrics.name: Primitive recursive relations via characteristic functions (Definition 137A)
rubrics_metrics.description: A relation R(⃗x) is primitive recursive iff its characteristic function χ_R(⃗x)=1 if R(⃗x) holds, 0 otherwise, is primitive recursive.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: IsZero(x) with χIsZero(0)=1, χIsZero(x+1)=0. Relations are handled by working with 0/1-valued primitive recursive functions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Closure of primitive recursive relations under Boolean operations (Proposition 137B)
rubrics_metrics.description: If P and Q are primitive recursive relations, then ¬P, P∧Q, P∨Q, P→Q are primitive recursive.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Define characteristic functions accordingly: χ¬P = 1 ˙− χP; χP∧Q = χP·χQ or min(χP,χQ); χP∨Q = max(χP,χQ); χP→Q = max(1 ˙− χP, χQ).

rubrics_metrics.name: Closure under bounded quantification (Proposition 137C)
rubrics_metrics.description: If R(⃗x,z) is primitive recursive, then (∀z<y) R(⃗x,z) and (∃z<y) R(⃗x,z) are primitive recursive.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Define χ_{∀}(⃗x,0)=1; χ_{∀}(⃗x,y+1)=min(χ_{∀}(⃗x,y), χ_R(⃗x,y)). Bounded existential uses max or is derived from bounded universal via negation. Conventions: (∀z<0) true, (∃z<0) false.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conditional function and definition by cases (cond and Proposition 137D)
rubrics_metrics.description: cond(x,y,z)=y if x=0, otherwise z; used to define functions by cases from primitive recursive relations/functions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: cond is defined by cond(0,y,z)=y, cond(x+1,y,z)=z. Use cond with characteristic functions to pick among g0,...,gm giving a piecewise-defined primitive recursive function.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bounded minimization (Proposition 138A)
rubrics_metrics.description: For primitive recursive relation R, m_R(⃗x,y) = least z<y with R(⃗x,z), if exists, and y otherwise, is primitive recursive.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Define by recursion: m_R(⃗x,0)=0; for y+1, cases depend on whether m_R(⃗x,y)≠y, or =y and R(⃗x,y) holds, otherwise y+1. Bounded search keeps result primitive recursive.

rubrics_metrics.name: Divisibility and primality as primitive recursive relations
rubrics_metrics.description: x | y ⇔ (∃z ≤ y) (x·z = y); Prime(x) ⇔ x≥2 ∧ (∀y ≤ x) (y|x → y=1 ∨ y=x).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use bounded quantification and arithmetic primitives to define divisibility and primality; nextPrime and the xth prime p(x) then obtained via bounded minimization and primitive recursion (Euclid's bound x!+1 gives effective bound).

rubrics_metrics.name: Coding finite sequences by prime-power encoding and primitive recursive sequence operations
rubrics_metrics.description: Encode ⟨a0,...,ak⟩ as ∏_{i=0}^k p_i^{a_i+1}; define len, append, element (s)i, concat, subseq as primitive recursive functions on codes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: len(s) uses a bounded minimization to find largest prime index dividing s; append(s,a)=2^{a+1}·s·p_{len(s)}^{a+1} (formal definition in text); element(s,i) uses min-a < s such that p_{a+1}^{i} ∤ s. sequenceBound(x,k)=p_{k−1}^{k·(x+1)} gives upper bounds for bounded searches.

rubrics_metrics.name: Concatenation and subsequence via bounded recursion
rubrics_metrics.description: Define helper hconcat(s,t,n) by primitive recursion to append first n symbols of t to s and then concat(s,t)=hconcat(s,t,len(t)); subseq(s,i,n) returns length-n subsequence beginning at i.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Can also define concat via bounded search using sequenceBound to bound the search; subseq and concat are primitive recursive (subseq left as exercise).

rubrics_metrics.name: Coding trees as sequences and SubtreeSeq primitive recursive (Proposition 1311A)
rubrics_metrics.description: Code tree as ⟨k, d1, ..., dk⟩ where k=number of immediate subtrees and di are codes of those subtrees; SubtreeSeq(t) returns sequence of codes of all subtrees of tree t and is primitive recursive.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Construct helper hSubtreeSeq(t,n) that builds level-n subtrees and use concatenation and sequence operations; maximum level ≤ code t, so take hSubtreeSeq(t,t) to get all subtrees.

rubrics_metrics.name: Other recursion schemas convertible to primitive recursion
rubrics_metrics.description: Simultaneous recursion (defining h0,h1 together), course-of-values recursion (h(⃗x,y+1)=g(⃗x,y,⟨h(⃗x,0),...,h(⃗x,y)⟩)), and parameter-changing recursion can all be simulated by ordinary primitive recursion using pairing/sequencing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use sequence coding and pairing to bundle multiple values/previous values into a single argument and then apply ordinary primitive recursion; examples and hints in text (e.g., course-of-values by passing the sequence ⟨h(...,0),...,h(...,y)⟩).

rubrics_metrics.name: Existence of computable but non-primitive recursive functions
rubrics_metrics.description: Diagonalization: enumerate unary primitive recursive functions f0,f1,... and define h(x)=f_x(x)+1, then h is computable but differs from every fi, so not primitive recursive. Ackermann–Péter function grows faster than any primitive recursive function.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Shows primitive recursive class is strict subset of computable functions; gives explicit growth-based examples (iterations g_n and G(x)=g_x(x) approximating Ackermann behavior).

rubrics_metrics.name: Enumeration of primitive recursive functions via coded notations
rubrics_metrics.description: Assign a natural number #(F) to each notation F recursively (#(0)=⟨0⟩, #(S)=⟨1⟩, #(Comp...), #(Recl[...])=⟨4,...⟩, etc.) to enumerate notations and hence associated functions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Some numbers do not code valid notations; define f_i to be the unary primitive recursive function coded by i if valid else constant 0. This explicit coding justifies the diagonalization argument and the computability of the universal enumerator g(x,y)=f_x(y).
